name: High Plains pivot over the Ogallala
headline: The well is the limiting factor. Every inch of pumping saved buys the farm more years.
story: A 125-acre centre pivot north of Garden City grows irrigated corn year after year. The water table under this county has dropped for decades, well yields are falling, and local management plans are tightening allocations. The question here is how to keep the pivot profitable on less water without leaving the silt loam bare to the spring wind.
challenge_tags: Wind and storm erosion on bare ground

baseline_rotation.name: Continuous irrigated corn
baseline_rotation.note: The Cropland Data Layer shows corn on this pivot in four of the last five years (sorghum once, in 2021).

water_context.in_situ_source: Kansas Geological Survey annual water-level measurements, southwest Kansas GMD3 (regional average, 2000-2023)
water_context.note: Saturated thickness in parts of this county has fallen by more than half since predevelopment. A Local Enhanced Management Area or water conservation area can cut allocations further.

corn.note: Feed yards and ethanol plants bid aggressively; corn often trades above the board here.

sorghum.note: Elevators, ethanol and export demand; usually a discount to corn.

winter_wheat.note: Every elevator takes hard red winter wheat.

soybean.note: Fewer delivery points than corn; check basis.

triticale.note: Dairies and feed yards nearby buy silage and hay; line up a buyer before seeding.

alfalfa.note: Strong dairy hay demand, but hay needs the most water of any option.

sunflower.note: Crush plant in Goodland, about 2.5 hours away.

canola.note: Limited delivery points; confirm a contract.

cotton.note: Gins operate in southwest Kansas, but needs a stripper and a short-season variety.
